pairs_diagnostics.cointegration_status_note: Formation spread does NOT reject the unit-root null at standard significance levels (Engle-Granger p = 0.1011, return correlation = 0.74). High return correlation does not establish cointegration; out-of-sample divergence risk is elevated.

parameter_surface.methodology_note: Evaluated K=25 parameter combinations across Entry Z-Score Threshold (σ) and Spread Z-Score Window (Days). Per Bailey & López de Prado (2014), the expected maximum Sharpe Ratio under a null hypothesis of zero skill across K=25 trials is 0.50. Inspect whether performance forms a broad plateau across neighbouring parameters or is isolated to a single spike.

literature_review.theoretical_mechanism_summary: This experiment investigates statistical arbitrage and relative-value convergence between KO and PEP using 'ols_log' spread construction (entry |z| >= 2.00, exit |z| <= 0.25). Following Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst (2006) and Engle & Granger (1987), pairs trading requires not merely price correlation, but a stationary cointegrated spread with a finite Ornstein-Uhlenbeck mean-reversion half-life. On the formation sample (2018-01-02 to 2021-12-29), the pair exhibits return correlation 0.74, ADF p-value 0.0314, and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck half-life 33.4 days.
literature_review.gemini_literature_synthesis: Empirical pairs trading studies (Do & Faff, 2010) emphasize two critical failure modes: (1) look-ahead bias when estimating hedge ratios on the full sample, and (2) out-of-sample structural breaks where diverging spreads fail to revert. Alpha Auditor locks OLS hedge ratio estimation strictly to the In-Sample formation window, charges 4 leg executions per round-trip, and enforces a |z| >= 4.0 divergence stop-loss.

strategy_papers.authors: Gatev, E., Goetzmann, W. N., & Rouwenhorst, K. G.
strategy_papers.title: Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative-Value Arbitrage Rule
strategy_papers.core_finding: Seminal empirical study testing two-standard-deviation spread divergence triggers between historically co-moving equities with strict formation vs. trading split separation.
strategy_papers.empirical_pitfall_warned: Estimating hedge ratios or spread standard deviations on the full sample introduces severe look-ahead bias that artificially guarantees mean reversion.
strategy_papers.how_alpha_auditor_addresses: Strictly estimates OLS hedge ratios on the In-Sample formation window (or causal rolling window) and applies two-leg transaction costs (4 executions per round-trip).

strategy_papers.authors: Engle, R. F., & Granger, C. W. J.
strategy_papers.title: Co-Integration and Error Correction: Representation, Estimation, and Testing
strategy_papers.core_finding: Establishes the formal two-step cointegration test demonstrating when a linear combination of two non-stationary I(1) price series forms a stationary I(0) equilibrium spread.
strategy_papers.empirical_pitfall_warned: High return correlation does not imply cointegration; two correlated random walks can diverge permanently without an error-correction mechanism.
strategy_papers.how_alpha_auditor_addresses: Computes Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF), Engle-Granger cointegration p-values, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck half-life of mean reversion, Hurst exponent, and Lo-MacKinlay Variance Ratio.

strategy_papers.title: Does Simple Pairs Trading Still Work?
strategy_papers.core_finding: Shows that cointegration relationships frequently experience structural breaks out-of-sample, causing diverging spreads that fail to revert.
strategy_papers.empirical_pitfall_warned: Pairs that appear cointegrated in-sample can suffer regime divergence out-of-sample when company fundamentals decouple.
strategy_papers.how_alpha_auditor_addresses: Enforces stop-loss z-score bounds (e.g., |z| >= 4.0) and executes a dedicated Out-of-Sample Spread Stability & Structural Break Stress Test in Step 5.

methodology_papers.title: The Statistics of Sharpe Ratios
methodology_papers.core_finding: Derives the asymptotic distribution and standard error of the Sharpe ratio under non-IID returns, accounting for serial correlation and higher-order moments.
methodology_papers.empirical_pitfall_warned: Assuming IID normal returns understates Sharpe ratio estimation error when strategies exhibit negative skewness or fat tails.
methodology_papers.how_alpha_auditor_addresses: Reports Lo (2002) / Mertens (2002) non-IID Sharpe standard errors and Probabilistic Sharpe Ratios (PSR) explicitly adjusted for sample skewness and kurtosis.

methodology_papers.authors: Bailey, D. H., & López de Prado, M.
methodology_papers.title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting, and Non-Normality
methodology_papers.core_finding: Quantifies the expected maximum Sharpe ratio under the null hypothesis across K independent parameter trials and deflates observed Sharpe ratios for multiple testing.
methodology_papers.empirical_pitfall_warned: Testing multiple parameter thresholds and cherry-picking the best historical setting inflates false-positive discovery rates.
methodology_papers.how_alpha_auditor_addresses: Tracks the exact number of parameter combinations K evaluated in the sensitivity grid and computes the Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) above the multiple-testing threshold E[max SR_0].

methodology_papers.authors: Politis, D. N., & Romano, J. P.
methodology_papers.title: The Stationary Bootstrap
methodology_papers.journal: Journal of the American Statistical Association, 89(428), 1303–1313
methodology_papers.core_finding: Constructs stationary resampled time series using geometrically distributed block lengths, preserving temporal dependence and volatility clustering.
methodology_papers.empirical_pitfall_warned: Standard IID bootstrap resampling destroys autocorrelation and GARCH volatility clusters in financial return series.
methodology_papers.how_alpha_auditor_addresses: Generates 95% confidence intervals for annualized return, Sharpe ratio, and mean trade return using Stationary Bootstrap resampling with automatic block-length selection.

methodology_papers.authors: Newey, W. K., & West, K. D.
methodology_papers.title: A Simple, Positive Semi-Definite, Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix
methodology_papers.core_finding: Provides a consistent covariance estimator for regression alpha and beta under serially correlated and heteroskedastic disturbances.
methodology_papers.empirical_pitfall_warned: OLS regression t-statistics on daily strategy returns are biased upward when residuals exhibit autocorrelation or volatility clustering.
methodology_papers.how_alpha_auditor_addresses: Estimates benchmark factor regressions using Newey-West HAC standard errors with automatic Bartlett kernel lag selection.

rigor_checklist.detail: Signals are computed strictly using data up to close of bar t; trade entry executes on bar t+1 (next_open) with 10.0 bps per-leg transaction cost.
First 50% of bars allocated to Formation/In-Sample; remaining 50% held out for Out-of-Sample validation.
Applies Lo (2002) / Mertens (2002) skewness-kurtosis Sharpe SE, Newey-West (1987) HAC alpha t-statistics, and Politis & Romano (1994) Stationary Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals.
Evaluates a 5×5 parameter neighborhood grid (K=25 trials) and reports the Bailey & López de Prado (2014) Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) relative to the expected maximum null Sharpe ratio.
All open, high, low, and close series are adjusted using split and dividend adjustment factors (AdjClose / Close) so historical splits do not create artificial price jumps.

stress_test_suite.gemini_overview: Gemini selected and executed 5 adversarial stress tests tailored to 'KO / PEP Statistical Arbitrage Spread Convergence' (pairs_cointegration_reversion / ols_log) on KO vs. PEP: (1) Right-Tail Outlier Trade Removal, (2) t+2 Execution Latency & 2×/3× Slippage Shock, (3) Realized Volatility & Bull/Bear Macro Regime Decomposition, (4) 500-Run Monte Carlo Random-Entry Null Benchmark, and (5) Out-of-Sample Cointegration Structural Break. Across the 5 stress tests, 0 showed high resilience, 0 showed moderate sensitivity, and 5 flagged high vulnerability.

tests.title: Right-Tail Outlier Concentration Test (Excl. Top 1 / 3 / 5 Trades)
tests.vulnerability_probed: Right-tail fragility: whether historical gains depend on 1–3 extreme outlier events.
tests.gemini_rationale: Short-horizon and event-driven strategies on KO frequently derive a disproportionate share of total return from crisis-rebound outliers (Nagel, 2012). This test removes the largest winners to verify whether the remaining signals still exhibit positive expectancy.
tests.methodology: Ranks all historical trades by net return, sequentially removes the top 1, 3, and 5 winning trades, and recalculates compounded net return and per-trade expectancy.
tests.key_finding: Across 66 historical trades, the single largest winning trade occurred on 2020-05-14 (+3.79% net). Removing the top 1 trade shifts compounded trade return from -23.95% to -26.73%; removing the top 3 winning trades results in -29.53% (mean trade return -0.540%).

tests.title: Execution Latency (t+2 Fill Delay) & Liquidity Slippage Shock
tests.vulnerability_probed: Microstructure decay & cost fragility: sensitivity to delayed order fills and widened bid-ask spreads.
tests.gemini_rationale: Jegadeesh (1990) and Park & Irwin (2007) show that many daily signals decay rapidly if execution is delayed by one bar or if bid-ask spreads widen during volatile sessions. We re-run the entire backtest with t+2 execution latency and 2×–3× transaction cost shocks.
tests.methodology: Shifts signal-to-fill latency from t+1 to t+2 bars and scales per-leg commission + slippage by 2× and 3× across the full historical sample.
tests.key_finding: Delaying trade execution by 1 additional trading day (filling at bar t+2 instead of t+1) changes cumulative net return from -23.95% (Sharpe -0.61) to -10.10% (Sharpe -0.22). Doubling transaction costs to 20 bps/leg yields -25.18% (Sharpe -0.70).

tests.title: Realized Volatility Terciles & Bull/Bear Macro Regime Breakdown
tests.vulnerability_probed: Regime dependency: whether returns only materialize in a single volatility or trend state.
tests.gemini_rationale: Strategies on KO can mask severe regime dependency in full-sample averages. We partition the historical sample by trailing 21-day realized volatility terciles and the 200-day benchmark trend filter to inspect conditional Sharpe stability.
tests.methodology: Classifies each trading bar into Low/Normal/High realized volatility terciles and Bull/Bear macro states (200-day SMA) and computes conditional net returns and annualized Sharpe ratios.
tests.key_finding: Strategy performance was positive in 0 of 5 tested volatility and macro regimes. In High Volatility periods (>17.0% ann. vol), the strategy returned -8.64% (Sharpe -0.45), compared to -8.40% (Sharpe -0.77) in Low Volatility periods (<11.1% ann. vol).

tests.title: Monte Carlo Random-Entry Null Benchmark (500 Non-Overlapping Simulations)
tests.vulnerability_probed: Passive drift vs. signal timing: whether non-overlapping random entries with matched durations, directions, and weights match the signal.
tests.gemini_rationale: On trending assets like KO, any directional rule can appear profitable simply by capturing unconditional market drift. We benchmark the user's exact trigger against 500 non-overlapping random-entry simulations matching all N=66 trade durations and directions.
tests.methodology: Draws 500 independent non-overlapping random-entry paths (matching the exact trade count N=66, holding-period distribution, trade directions, leg weights, next_open fills, and costs) to compute an empirical signal-timing p-value and Monte Carlo standard error.
tests.key_finding: Across 500 non-overlapping Monte Carlo simulations matching the exact multiset of 66 trade durations (mean 12d), directions, fill timing (next_open), and transaction costs, the median random-entry return was -14.44% (10th–90th percentile: [-28.82%, +1.09%]). The hypothesis signal's actual return (-23.95%) ranked at the 20.0th percentile (empirical one-sided p = 0.800 ± 0.018).

tests.title: Out-of-Sample Hedge Ratio Drift & Cointegration Breakdown Test
tests.vulnerability_probed: Cointegration regime break: whether the two assets decouple out-of-sample (Do & Faff, 2010).
tests.gemini_rationale: Pairs trading between KO and PEP assumes a stable equilibrium spread. We test whether the formation hedge ratio β and spread stationarity survive in the held-out sample.
tests.methodology: Re-estimates the OLS cointegrating regression on the Out-of-Sample split to measure hedge-ratio parameter drift (Δβ%) and out-of-sample Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) stationarity.
tests.key_finding: Between the In-Sample formation period and Out-of-Sample trading period, the optimal OLS hedge ratio β between KO and PEP shifted by 181.8% (0.687 → -0.561). Out-of-sample spread ADF stationarity p-value is 0.8966 (vs. 0.0314 in-sample).

scorecard.hypothesis_restatement: KO / PEP Statistical Arbitrage Spread Convergence
scorecard.executive_summary: Historical Audit Summary for 'KO / PEP Statistical Arbitrage Spread Convergence': Across 2011 trading days (2018-01-02 to 2025-12-31), the specified rule triggered 66 trades (In-Sample N = 36, Out-of-Sample N = 30), generating -23.95% net return (Sharpe -0.61, Max Drawdown 25.83%) versus +187.48% (Sharpe 0.78) for passive SPY Buy-and-Hold (-211.43 percentage points excess return). The 25.0% portfolio drawdown circuit breaker tripped on 2025-07-17. Econometrically, KO and PEP exhibit daily return correlation r = +0.739, while the log-price spread ADF stationarity test yields p = 0.0314 (stationary cointegrated spread). The trading rule satisfied 0 of 5 evaluated empirical checks (CONTRADICTED BY HISTORICAL DATA). Note: This scorecard summarizes historical sample evidence using explicit heuristic decision thresholds and does not constitute investment advice or a prediction of future performance.
key_takeaways: Direction & Expectancy: 66 trades averaged -0.398% net with a 53.0% win rate and 25.83% max drawdown.
In-Sample vs. Out-of-Sample: Formation Sharpe was 0.01 (-0.47% across 36 trades); Out-of-Sample Sharpe was -1.45 (-23.59% across 30 trades).
Benchmark Factor Decomposition: Annualized Newey-West HAC alpha is -3.15% (t = -1.78, p = 0.075) with market beta β = -0.009.
Co-Movement vs. Cointegration Distinction: Daily returns correlate at r = +0.739, but log-spread stationarity has ADF p = 0.0314 (Hurst H = 0.467).

dimensions.name: 1. Post-Signal Direction & Net Trade Expectancy
dimensions.question: Did historical occurrences of the signal produce positive average returns after transaction costs?
dimensions.evidence_metric: Mean Net Trade: -0.398% | Win Rate: 53.0% (N = 66 trades)
dimensions.explanation: Across 66 historical signals from 2018-01-02 to 2025-12-31, the average trade returned -0.398% net (-13.18% cumulative gross, -23.95% cumulative net). Heuristic classification requires N >= 5 trades and positive net mean/cumulative return for SUPPORTED.

dimensions.name: 2. Statistical Significance vs. Noise (Lo 2002 PSR & Newey-West HAC)
dimensions.question: Is the observed return/Sharpe ratio statistically distinguishable from random noise?
dimensions.explanation: After adjusting for sample skewness (-0.69) and Pearson kurtosis (26.44) via Lo (2002), the Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio is 4.0%. Benchmark factor regression yields annualized alpha of -3.15% (Newey-West HAC t = -1.78, p = 0.075). Heuristic hurdle: PSR >= 85% and HAC p <= 0.10 (or t-test p <= 0.05).

dimensions.name: 3. Held-Out Out-of-Sample Persistence
dimensions.question: Did the hypothesis continue to hold in the unseen Out-of-Sample validation period?
dimensions.explanation: In the held-out validation sample (2021-12-30 to 2025-12-31), the strategy executed 30 trades with net return -23.59% and Sharpe ratio -1.45 (vs. 0.01 In-Sample). Heuristic hurdle: N_OOS >= 3 trades, positive OOS net return, and OOS SR > 0.20.

dimensions.explanation: Deducting 10.0 bps per unit of portfolio notional shifts full-sample return from -13.18% (gross) to -23.95% (net). Estimated break-even cost is 0.0 bps one-way.

dimensions.explanation: Out of 5 adversarial stress tests in Step 5, the hypothesis scored Resilient on 0 and flagged High Vulnerability on 5.

calculation_steps.title: Step A — Compounded Net Trade Return, Unit Gross Exposure & Running-Peak Drawdown
calculation_steps.formula: R_{net,i} = R_{gross,i} − 2·c,   |w_A| + |w_B| = 1.0,   E_0 = C_0,   H_t = max(E_0, max_{1 ≤ s ≤ t} E_s),   D_t = 1 − (E_t / H_t)
calculation_steps.substituted_inputs: Initial Capital E_0 = $100,000.00, Unit gross exposure (|w_A| + |w_B| = 1.0), c_comm = 5.0 bps, c_slip = 5.0 bps ⇒ Round-trip cost = 20.0 bps (0.200%/trade) across N = 66 trades; Circuit Breaker Limit = 25.0%
calculation_steps.output_value: Gross = -13.18% → Net = -23.95% (Mean Net/Trade = -0.398%) | Max Drawdown = 25.83% (IS = 9.15%, OOS = 23.96%)
calculation_steps.interpretation: Every trade deducts round-trip commission + slippage on unit gross notional, and running peak H_t anchors at initial capital E_0 so immediate day-1 losses are captured (reported as positive loss magnitude D_t ∈ [0%, 100%] in tables and U_t = −D_t ≤ 0% on underwater charts).

calculation_steps.title: Step B — Annualized Sharpe Ratio & Lo (2002) / Mertens (2002) Non-IID Standard Error
calculation_steps.substituted_inputs: T = 2011 days, Ann. Vol = 5.36%, Skewness γ₃ = -0.690, Pearson Kurtosis γ₄ = 26.441
calculation_steps.output_value: Annualized SR = -0.614, Lo (2002) SE = 0.351, Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio PSR(0) = 4.0%
calculation_steps.interpretation: Adjusts standard Sharpe inference for non-normal fat tails and skewness so negative-skew strategies are not overstated.

calculation_steps.title: Step C — Bailey & López de Prado (2014) Multiple-Testing Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR)
calculation_steps.formula: E[max SR₀] ≈ √V[{SR_k}] × [(1 − γ)·Φ⁻¹(1 − 1/K) + γ·Φ⁻¹(1 − 1/(K·e))],   DSR = Φ((SR − E[max SR₀]) / SE(SR))
calculation_steps.substituted_inputs: K = 25 parameter grid trials, Null Hurdle E[max SR₀] = 0.497 (annualized)
calculation_steps.interpretation: Penalizes the observed Sharpe ratio for the number of parameter combinations explored in the 5×5 sensitivity grid.

calculation_steps.title: Step D — Newey-West (1987) HAC Benchmark Factor Decomposition
calculation_steps.formula: R_strat,t = α + β · R_bench,t + ε_t,   Var_HAC(hat(α)) = T⁻¹ (X'X)⁻¹ hat(Ω)_NW (X'X)⁻¹
calculation_steps.substituted_inputs: Benchmark = SPY, Bartlett kernel lags L = 7, Sample T = 2011 daily return pairs
calculation_steps.interpretation: Separates passive correlation with the benchmark (β) from excess timing return (α) using autocorrelation-consistent standard errors.

calculation_steps.title: Step E — Cointegrated Spread & Exact Discrete Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Half-Life
calculation_steps.formula: S_t = log(P_A,t) − (hat(α) + hat(β)·log(P_B,t)),   ΔS_t = ϕ + λ·S_{t−1} + η_t,   t_{1/2} = −ln(2) / ln(1 + λ)
calculation_steps.output_value: ADF Stat = -3.039 (p = 0.0314), Half-Life t_{1/2} = 33.4 days, Hurst H = 0.467
calculation_steps.interpretation: Formation spread does NOT reject the unit-root null at standard significance levels (Engle-Granger p = 0.1011, return correlation = 0.74). High return correlation does not establish cointegration; out-of-sample divergence risk is elevated.

methodology_notes: Causal Signal & Execution Timing: Signals are evaluated strictly at the close of bar t using data [0..t] and executed at bar t+1 (next_open) with 5.0 bps commission + 5.0 bps adverse slippage per unit of portfolio notional.

Chronological Holdout Separation: Dataset (2011 trading days) is partitioned into an In-Sample Formation split (2018-01-02 to 2021-12-29, 1006 days) and a Held-Out Out-of-Sample split (2021-12-30 to 2025-12-31, 1005 days).

Inference under Non-Normality & Serial Dependence: Sharpe Ratio standard errors and Probabilistic Sharpe Ratios (PSR) incorporate sample skewness and kurtosis per Mertens (2002) and Lo (2002). Confidence intervals use the Politis & Romano (1994) Stationary Bootstrap, and benchmark alpha/beta t-statistics use Newey-West (1987) HAC standard errors.

Pairs Cointegration Formation: Within the Formation split (2018-01-02 to 2021-12-29), OLS parameters (alpha_t, beta_t) are estimated causally on expanding windows [0..t] to eliminate in-sample look-ahead bias, then frozen at the full Formation estimates (beta = 0.6866, alpha = 0.5088) throughout Out-of-Sample evaluation.
limitations: Historical Simulation Boundary: Historical backtests and statistical significance measures describe past price paths and do not guarantee future market behaviour or liquidity.

Execution & Microstructure Simplification: Fills are modelled at daily Open/Close bars with fixed basis-point slippage and do not model intraday limit-order-book queue priority, borrow fee spikes on short legs, or market impact for large notional orders.

Selection & Multiple-Testing Bias: Inspecting multiple thresholds or re-running hypotheses on the same dataset increases false-discovery probability; consult the Bailey & López de Prado (2014) Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) and Out-of-Sample split metrics when interpreting results.
